name: Te'un
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Taber, Mark. 1993. Toward a better understanding of the indigenous languages of Southwestern Maluku. Oceanic Linguistics 32(2): 389-441 -- Teun 193-item list as digitised in LexiRumah 3.0.0 (Kaiping, Edwards & Klamer 2019, lect teun1241) and ABVD language 303
sources.note: Primary data only: phonetic forms carry Taber's stress marks. My tabulation : 167 penult, 12 final (mostly prefixed verbs with reduced roots: anˈti 'eat', tɔnˈla 'see', nafˈre 'know'; waˈti 'what', seˈwo 'who'), 2 antepenult, 11 monosyllables. The article's own prose (any transcription/stress note) not accessible (JSTOR paywall).

sources.citation: Stokhof, W.A.L. (ed.) 1981. Holle lists vol. 3/2: Central Moluccas: Seram (II). Pacific Linguistics D-44. List 224b 'Niala' (Boemei, 1937), pp. 161-174 [= Teun of Bumei village per Edwards 2025 fn.5, Grimes & Edwards 2026:217 fn.23]
sources.note: Bare wordlist in Dutch-style spelling, no stress marks, no phonetic notes.

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. & Owen Edwards. 2026. The Austronesian languages of eastern Indonesia and Timor-Leste: Unravelling their prehistory and classification. Berlin: Language Science Press. sec. 4.6.4 Teun-Nila-Serua, pp. 217-223
sources.note: Historical phonology only (Yafila Teun data from Edwards 2023a, cited without stress marks); no statement on Teun stress; only the generic remark p.115 'penultimate stress is the normal rule for Wallacean languages'.

sources.citation: Edwards, Owen. 2025. Teun, Nila, Serua (Indonesia) - a collection of language snapshots. Language Documentation and Description 25(1): 1-12. DOI 10.25894/ldd.2615
sources.note: Nothing. p.7 'Previous research' gives the complete Teun bibliography: Taber 1993 (190-item list), Erniata & Wijaya 2023 (phrases), Pasapan et al. 2022 (Kantor Bahasa dictionary), Stokhof 1981 Holle list 224b; notes Chlenova 2006 is on Wetan of Layeni, not Teun.

sources.citation: Edwards, Owen. 2023-. Emplawas and languages of the Babar islands (ELDP IPF0417), Endangered Languages Archive: remaining Teun bundles (texts recorded July 2024; any future Teun sketch or phonology notes), hdl:2196/28f40694-81ac-4d06-b515-617dd6469394
sources.note: Edwards is the only linguist currently working on Teun; a sketch or transcription-conventions document (as exists for Emplawas) would give a first-hand stress statement; audio permits instrumental verification.

sources.citation: Edwards, Owen. 2023. Teun wordlist / Daftar kata bahasa Teun (bundle TVE001, Yafila, Dec 2023), collection 'Emplawas and languages of the Babar islands' (ELDP IPF0417), Endangered Languages Archive, hdl:2196/419b6d34-b044-4f86-a864-beaabb8b0bda: typed 505-item list) and 12-pp scan of handwritten field form)
sources.note: No statement. Typed list is phonemic without stress marks (one phonetic [ˈʔiʔiː]); the handwritten field form marks stress on phonetic forms (p.1 ˈtɛfu, ˈliwa, ˈsɔu, ˈmnarsa, ˈfiwa, maˈmama, ˈwari, ˈlɔtna, ˈskɛra), overwhelmingly penultimate. Data only.

sources.citation: Erniati & Dendi Wijaya. 2023. Frasa verbal bahasa Teon di Pulau Seram. Kibas Cenderawasih 20(2): 195-208. DOI 10.26499/kc.v20i2.420
sources.note: Nothing; verbal-phrase syntax of Watludan Teon only.

sources.citation: Erniati & Mudarsep. 2022. Klasifikasi pola frasa ajektival bahasa Teon. Kibas Cenderawasih 19(2): 143-159.

sources.note: Nothing; confirms the dictionary project (speakers from Watludan, Yafila, Mesa); no PDF link.

sources.citation: van Engelenhoven, Aone. 2003. Language endangerment in Indonesia: The incipient obsolescence and acute death of Teun, Nila and Serua (Central and Southwest Maluku). In Janse & Tol (eds.), Language Death and Language Maintenance (CILT 240), 49-80. Amsterdam: Benjamins.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Phoneme inventory and typological notes are for Serua only; Teun appears in sociolinguistics and one possessive-paradigm row (p.55). Nothing on stress for any TNS variety.

sources.citation: Collins, James T. 1982. Prothesis in the languages of Central Maluku. PL C-75: 187-200
sources.note: Only a provenance note on the 'Niala' Holle list; nothing on Teun stress.
